patients.summary: Young apprentice electrician with childhood ADHD on methylphenidate and post-concussive syndrome after a mild TBI at 19, a daily smoker and heavy episodic drinker. Three high-speed car crashes in 16 months: a right posterior hip dislocation (2025), diffuse axonal injury with recovery (Dec 2025), and a severe diffuse axonal injury with coma (Aug 2026); he is in the ICU at today and the practice knows it mostly from his mother.

documents.title: New Patient Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
20M here to set up primary care. His old office was a pediatric-and-family practice he aged out of; he wants someone to keep his ADHD prescription going.

HPI: ADHD, combined type, diagnosed as a kid. On methylphenidate ER 36 mg every morning for years, says it lets him get through a workday on site and keep his apprenticeship classes straight. No chest pain, palpitations or fainting on it. Appetite down at lunch, eats a big dinner. Sleeps 6-7 h.
At 19 he had a concussion (mild TBI). Afterward had headaches and was short-tempered and low for a while; the old office started sertraline 50 mg and he has stayed on it. Feels it keeps him level. Headaches now come and go, he takes ibuprofen 600 a few times a month. No vision change, no weakness.

PMH: ADHD, combined. Mild TBI at 19 with lingering post-concussive symptoms.
PSH: T&A age 8. Left distal radius fracture at 19, ORIF; plate still in, no wrist complaints.
Meds: methylphenidate ER 36 mg qAM; sertraline 50 mg daily; ibuprofen 600 mg q6h prn headache.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: father with alcohol use disorder and high blood pressure. Mother with depression and hypothyroidism. Older brother has ADHD and a learning disability.
SH: apprentice electrician, union program. Cigarettes daily, about a pack a day, started around 18. Alcohol on weekends and sometimes midweek, usually 5-6 drinks when he goes out, 2-3 nights a week. No drug use reported.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet. Well appearing, fidgety but engaged. HEENT clear, tonsils surgically absent. Neck supple. Heart RRR no murmur. Lungs clear bilaterally. Abdomen soft, nontender. Left wrist healed volar scar, full motion. Neuro: alert, oriented, CN II-XII intact, strength and reflexes symmetric, gait normal.
PHQ-9 4, GAD-7 3, AUDIT-C 8.

A/P:
1. ADHD, combined type - continue methylphenidate ER 36 mg qAM. Controlled-substance agreement reviewed and signed today; state PMP checked, single prescriber, fills monthly as expected. 30-day e-scripts, follow-up every 3-6 months.
2. Post-concussive syndrome - stable, continue sertraline 50 mg and ibuprofen prn. Counseled to keep ibuprofen to the lowest use that works.
3. Tobacco - smoking about a pack a day. Talked about quitting, offered patch or a quitline referral; not ready. Will revisit.
4. Alcohol - AUDIT-C 8, binge pattern. Discussed risks, especially with the family history and with his stimulant. He listened, does not want to cut back right now.
5. Health maintenance - CBC, CMP, lipids, one-time HIV and hep C screens today. Flu shot given. Requesting old records for the vaccine history.
RTC 3 months.

documents.title: Controlled Substance Agreement
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Controlled substance agreement for methylphenidate ER reviewed with patient by MA and PCP. Patient agrees: one prescriber (this office), one pharmacy, no early refills, no sharing or selling medication, lost or stolen prescriptions not replaced early, periodic PMP review. Patient signed; copy given. Scanned to chart.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Josue, your blood work from yesterday looks good - blood counts, kidney and liver tests normal. LDL cholesterol is a little above ideal, nothing to treat at 20; cutting the cigarettes would do more for your heart than anything else. The HIV and hepatitis C screens were negative. See you in February.

- Office visit after a concussion at age 19: headaches and poor sleep, later irritability and low mood; sertraline 50 mg daily started at a follow-up, reported helpful.
- Left distal radius ORIF at age 19 noted in history; operative report not included in packet.
- T&A age 8.
- Immunizations: childhood series complete. Tdap and MenACWY 10/2013, HPV 9-valent 10/2013 and 5/2014 (2-dose series complete), MenACWY booster 1/2019.
- No known drug allergies.
Forwarded to PCP for review.

events.reason: Right hip pain after motor vehicle collision

conditions.label: Posterior dislocation of right hip, initial encounter

documents.title: Emergency Department Record (outside)
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital emergency department. Date of service 04/06/2025. Received 04/30/2025 in response to records request.

CC: R hip pain after MVC.
HPI: 22 yo M arrived by EMS after a high-speed crash; he was the front passenger, no seatbelt. Per EMS the vehicle hit a guardrail and spun off the road into a ditch. Awake and talking on scene. Complains of severe right hip pain, could not stand. Denies striking his head, denies LOC, denies abdominal pain.
PMH ADHD, prior mild TBI at 19 with post-concussive syndrome. PSH L distal radius ORIF, T&A. Meds methylphenidate ER 36 qAM, sertraline 50 daily, ibuprofen 600 prn. NKDA. Smokes 1 ppd. Drinks heavily on weekends.

Exam: GCS 15. No scalp or facial injury. C-spine cleared clinically. Chest and abdomen atraumatic, nontender. Pelvis stable. R lower extremity shortened, hip held internally rotated; any passive movement painful. No thigh swelling, deformity, wound or bleeding. Sensation intact in sciatic, femoral and obturator distributions; DP/PT pulses 2+; foot dorsiflexion and plantarflexion intact.

Imaging: AP pelvis - right femoral head displaced posteriorly and superiorly out of the acetabulum, consistent with posterior hip dislocation. No fracture seen.
Orthopedics consulted from the ED.

Procedure: closed reduction of R hip under procedural sedation by ED with orthopedics at bedside, successful on first attempt. Tolerated well.
Post-reduction AP pelvis: concentric reduction. CT pelvis post-reduction: right hip concentrically reduced; no acetabular or femoral head fracture; no intra-articular fragment.
Post-reduction neurovascular exam unchanged, intact.

Disposition: discharged home 09:50 with crutches, WBAT, posterior hip precautions reviewed (no deep flexion, no crossing legs, no internal rotation). Continue home ibuprofen for pain. Orthopedics clinic in 1-2 weeks. Seatbelt counseling given.
Dx: posterior dislocation of right hip, reduced.
Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: Patient call - ED visit over the weekend
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Pt calling. Was a passenger in a car crash early Sunday morning, his right hip "popped out" and they put it back in at the ED and sent him home. On crutches. Pain manageable with ibuprofen. No numbness in leg or foot, no head injury. Needs a note for work and wants to be seen. ED told him to see ortho, he has a number to call. Booked with PCP Wed 4/9. Advised ED for new numbness, worsening pain, or foot weakness.

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Office Visit - post-ED follow-up
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
22M seen after ED visit on 4/6. No ED records yet - history from patient.
He was the front passenger; not belted. Right hip dislocated, reduced in the ED under sedation, told no fracture on x-ray and CT. Sent home same morning on crutches.
Since then: hip sore but better each day, ibuprofen 600 two or three times a day helps. Using crutches, putting some weight on the leg. No numbness, tingling or foot drop. Didn't hit his head. No headache beyond his usual.

Exam: vitals reviewed. Uncomfortable getting on table. R hip - no bruising over the lateral thigh, ROM deferred. Sensation intact to light touch R foot and leg, ankle dorsiflexion and great toe extension 5/5, DP pulse 2+.

A/P: R posterior hip dislocation s/p closed reduction 4/6.
- Ortho follow-up - he has the clinic number, will call today. Reviewed hip precautions.
- Pain: ibuprofen 600 q6h prn with food, max 4/day; short course ok.
- Work note: off work through ortho visit.
- Requesting ED record.
- Seatbelt - every time. He agreed.
RTC after ortho, ~6-8 wk.

documents.title: Orthopedic Clinic Letter (outside)
documents.author: orthopedics
documents.body:
Outside orthopedics group. Visit 04/23/2025. Received 05/01/2025.

Re: Josue Hernandez, DOB 08/31/2002

Thank you for following this patient. He is a 22 year old seen 17 days after closed reduction of a right posterior hip dislocation from a car crash. He has been walking with crutches, partial weight, and the pain is steadily better.

Exam: walks with crutches, mild antalgic gait. R hip flexion to 90 with mild discomfort at end range, internal rotation not tested per precautions. No sciatic nerve deficit: EHL, tibialis anterior and gastrocnemius 5/5, sensation intact in the foot. Distal pulses palpable.
AP pelvis today: right hip concentrically reduced. No fracture.

Impression: right posterior hip dislocation, simple, status post closed reduction, recovering as expected.
Plan: wean off crutches over the next 1-2 weeks as comfort allows. Posterior precautions to 6 weeks from injury. Light duty may begin now (no ladders, no lifting over 20 lb); full duty from 05/19/2025. Return to this clinic as needed.
Meds: methylphenidate ER, sertraline, ibuprofen prn. Allergies: NKDA.

documents.title: ED record received
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: ED record from 4/6 visit received by fax after second request. Filed under the ED encounter and routed to PCP.

documents.title: Outside ED record reviewed
documents.author: PCP

documents.title: RE: Work note for full duty

events.reason: Head injury after motor vehicle collision

conditions.label: Diffuse traumatic brain injury with loss of consciousness of unspecified duration, initial encounter
conditions.note: Diffuse axonal injury on CT, GCS 13 on arrival

reports.text:
Indication: high-speed MVC, loss of consciousness, GCS 13.
Technique: axial noncontrast CT of the head with bone and soft tissue reconstructions.
Findings: multiple tiny punctate foci of hemorrhage scattered in the cerebral white matter, with blurring of the gray-white matter junction. No extra-axial collection. No large intraparenchymal hematoma. No midline shift. Ventricles and basal cisterns normal in size and configuration. No skull fracture. Paranasal sinuses and mastoids clear. Forehead soft tissue swelling.
reports.conclusion: Numerous punctate hemorrhages with blurred gray-white junction, consistent with diffuse axonal injury. No skull fracture or large intracranial hematoma.

reports.text:
Indication: follow-up of diffuse axonal injury.
Comparison: CT head 12/04/2025.
Findings: the small punctate hemorrhagic foci are unchanged in number and size. No new hemorrhage. No mass effect or midline shift. Ventricles stable. No skull fracture.
reports.conclusion: Stable appearance of punctate hemorrhages. No new intracranial hemorrhage.

documents.title: Hospital Discharge Summary (outside)
documents.author: trauma surgery
documents.body:
Regional hospital - Trauma Surgery. Admitted 12/04/2025, discharged 12/07/2025. Received 01/08/2026 after records request.

Admitting diagnosis: traumatic brain injury after MVC.
Discharge diagnosis: diffuse axonal injury.

History: 23 yo man brought in after a high-speed crash; unrestrained driver, lost consciousness at the scene per EMS. Background of ADHD and a mild TBI at 19 with post-concussive syndrome, and an ED visit in April 2025 for a right posterior hip dislocation.
Arrival: BP 130/85, HR 102, RR 18, T 37.1. GCS 13 - confused, agitated, not oriented. Abrasion across the forehead, no other external injury. Pupils equal, reactive. Moving all four limbs, no focal neurologic deficit.
CT head: multiple small punctate hemorrhages with loss of gray-white distinction, no fracture or large hematoma - diffuse axonal injury. CBC and BMP unremarkable.

Course: admitted to trauma ICU for hourly neuro checks. Repeat CT head next morning stable. Neurosurgery reviewed images, no operative need. Mental status cleared, GCS 15 by afternoon of 12/05. Transferred to floor 12/06. Ambulating independently, tolerating diet. Home methylphenidate held while inpatient, resumed at discharge.

Discharge meds: methylphenidate ER 36 mg qAM, sertraline 50 mg daily, ibuprofen 600 mg q6h prn headache.
Allergies: NKDA.
Instructions: no driving and no return to work until cleared at follow-up. Rest, limited screens first days, gradual return to activity. Avoid alcohol. Return for worsening headache, vomiting, confusion, weakness or seizure. Follow up with PCP within 1 week; outpatient neurology/brain injury clinic referral recommended.
Discharged home with family.

documents.title: Call from mother - hospital discharge
documents.author: RN
documents.body:
Patient's mother called (pt with her, gave verbal ok to speak with her). He was in another car accident Thursday night, he was driving. Hit his head, kept in the ICU then the floor, discharged yesterday. They said there was bleeding "in small spots" in the brain. No surgery. At home he has a headache and is sleeping a lot but is making sense, eating, walking fine. No vomiting. Discharge papers say see PCP in a week.
Reviewed red flags: worsening headache, repeated vomiting, confusion, weakness, seizure -> 911/ED. Booked with PCP Thu 12/11. Asked them to bring discharge paperwork.

procedures.procedure: Transitional care management, moderate complexity

documents.title: Post-hospital visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
23M, here with his mother, 4 days after discharge from a 12/4-12/7 admission after a second high-speed crash (this time he was the driver, not belted). Only the patient instructions sheet came with him; no discharge summary yet.
Per the sheet and family: lost consciousness at the scene, CT showed diffuse axonal injury (small bleeds), ICU overnight, repeat CT stable, no surgery, back to normal thinking the next day.

Now: headaches most days since discharge, ibuprofen takes the edge off. Tired, napping. Can follow a TV show but focus fades by late afternoon. No vomiting, no vision change, no weakness, no seizure. Methylphenidate restarted at discharge. Sertraline continued. Not driving. Not drinking since.

Exam: vitals reviewed. Alert, oriented x3, answers appropriately, a bit slow. Healing abrasion forehead, no swelling. Pupils equal, reactive. EOMI, no nystagmus. Face symmetric. Strength 5/5 all limbs, reflexes symmetric, finger-nose normal, gait steady, Romberg negative. GCS 15.
PHQ-9 5.

A/P:
1. Diffuse axonal injury after MVC 12/4 - recovering, nonfocal exam. Added to problem list. Relative rest with gradual return to activity; ibuprofen prn, limit to a few days a week to avoid rebound. No driving until neurology clears him. Off work until early January - note given. Neurology referral placed. Requesting the hospital records.
2. Post-concussive syndrome (from age 19) - expect headaches to be worse for a while.
3. ADHD - continue methylphenidate ER 36 mg.
4. Alcohol - strongly advised to stay off alcohol while the brain heals; he says he will.
5. Seatbelt.
RTC 3 months or sooner.

documents.title: Work note
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: To whom it may concern: Josue Hernandez is under my care following a hospitalization. He is unable to work through 01/04/2026. I expect he can return to light duty on 01/05/2026, with no work at heights or with live circuits until further notice. Please contact the office with any questions.

documents.author: PCP
documents.body: That's the direction we want. Yes, light duty on the ground from 1/5 is fine - no ladders, lifts or live work yet, and take breaks when the fatigue hits. No driving until neurology sees you. The neurology office should call you to schedule; let us know if you haven't heard by the first week of January.

documents.body:
Follow-up 3 months after the December diffuse axonal injury.
Neurology: seen once, early February. No note has come to us despite the request. Per patient, they told him he was recovering well, could go back to full duty and could drive again. Full duty since late February.
Headaches back to his old pattern, a couple a month, ibuprofen prn. Energy normal. Focus back to where it was on methylphenidate. Mood ok. Back to drinking on weekends, 5-6 when he goes out. Smoking a pack daily.

Exam: vitals per flowsheet. Alert, oriented, conversational, quick. Forehead healed. CN II-XII intact, strength and coordination normal, gait and tandem normal.
PHQ-9 3. AUDIT-C 8.

A/P:
1. Diffuse axonal injury 12/2025 - back to baseline, marking resolved. Neurology referral closed on his report.
2. Post-concussive syndrome - unchanged, continue sertraline 50 and ibuprofen prn.
3. ADHD - continue methylphenidate ER 36 mg.
4. Alcohol and tobacco - two serious crashes in a year. Long talk about drinking, driving, seatbelts. Offered referral again; he will think about it.
RTC 3 mo (video ok).

documents.title: Video Visit - medication check
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Video, pt at home, ID confirmed.
No new issues. Methylphenidate ER 36 working, no side effects. Mood fine. Headaches infrequent. Working full time.
Still smoking, still drinking on weekends - declines help today.
Plan: continue methylphenidate ER 36 mg and sertraline 50 mg. PMP checked. Physical in the fall.

reports.text:
Indication: MVC, unresponsive, GCS 6.
Comparison: CT head 12/05/2025.
Findings: no acute intracranial hemorrhage. No extra-axial collection. Gray-white differentiation preserved. No sulcal effacement, no cerebral edema. Ventricles and cisterns normal. No midline shift. No skull fracture.
reports.conclusion: No skull fracture, intracranial hemorrhage or cerebral edema.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record (outside)
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Regional hospital ED. DOS 08/02/2026. Received 08/20/2026 in response to records request. Inpatient records not included.

CC: MVC, unresponsive.
HPI: 23 yo M, unrestrained driver in a high-speed collision with extensive driver-side damage per EMS. Unresponsive on EMS arrival and on ours. Hx per chart: ADHD; diffuse axonal injury 12/2025; mild TBI at 19 with post-concussive syndrome; R posterior hip dislocation 4/2025. Meds methylphenidate ER, sertraline, ibuprofen prn. NKDA.

Primary survey: airway not protected, GCS 6. Intubated on arrival for airway protection, rapid sequence, first pass, tube position confirmed.
Secondary: pupils equal and reactive. No palpable skull fracture or scalp step-off. No lateralizing findings. Chest, abdomen and pelvis without external trauma.
CT head: no fracture, no hemorrhage, no edema. CBC and BMP within normal limits.

Course: despite the negative CT he remains comatose off sedation pauses, with intermittent decerebrate posturing. Neurosurgery and trauma consulted.
Impression: severe traumatic brain injury, clinical picture of diffuse axonal injury with normal CT.
Disposition: admitted to trauma ICU 04:35, intubated.

orders.order: Records request, regional hospital ED and inpatient, 08/2026

documents.title: Call from mother - patient hospitalized
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Mother called to let us know Josue was in another crash early Sunday, driving. He is in the ICU on a breathing machine and has not woken up. She says the scan didn't show bleeding but the doctors are worried about the brain. She wanted his doctor to know. Offered support. PCP made aware. Records request faxed to the hospital.

documents.title: RE: Call from mother - patient hospitalized
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Called mother back. Said I'm sorry, and that we'll be here for whatever she and he need. She has the ICU team's contact; I gave her our direct line. Will review records when they arrive.

documents.author: MA
documents.body: Automated refill request from pharmacy for methylphenidate ER 36 mg #30.

documents.title: RE: Pharmacy refill request - methylphenidate
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Denied - patient currently hospitalized. Pharmacy notified to inactivate auto-refill.

documents.title: Outside ED record reviewed
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: ED record from 8/2 received; inpatient notes still outstanding. Unrestrained driver, GCS 6, intubated on arrival, CT head negative, comatose with intermittent decerebrate posturing - severe diffuse axonal injury. Admitted to trauma ICU. Records request stays open for the admission.

documents.title: Call from mother - ICU update
documents.author: RN
documents.body: Mother called. He is still in the ICU, still not awake, still on the breathing machine. The ICU team asked her for his medication list and past history. With PCP approval, faxed med list, problem list, allergies and recent visit note to the ICU fax number on the unit's paperwork she read to us. Mother thanked us.
